mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be negative due to persistent discount rate expectations and reduced liquidity in credit markets.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the mean of the pre-trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in CPIAUCSL by at least 0.5% followed by a stabilization signals disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as rate-cut expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL drops ≥ 0.5% in a month then remains flat for the next month
failure_condition: Over 12 such triggers, the average 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS of at least 2% above the prior month's level, sustained for two consecutive months, predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as labor market strength supports equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases ≥ 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 10 such events, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 grows by more than 10% in a quarter compared to the prior quarter, accompanied by a simultaneous rise in HOUST by at least 5%, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be positive due to strong consumer and business demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > 10% AND HOUST monthly increase ≥ 5% in the same quarter
failure_condition: In 20 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 3% followed by a sustained rise of at least 2% in the same month predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as weak industrial production coincides with reduced market optimism.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls ≥ 3% in a month then rises ≥ 2% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 10 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.0% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be positive as lower unemployment expectations reduce risk aversion.
failure_condition: Across 15 such regimes, the average 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS exceeding 5% for two consecutive months suggests excess demand for safe assets, which is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to flight to quality.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases ≥ 5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 12 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS exceeds 160,000 in a month and UNRATE is below 4% simultaneously, the S&P 500 forward 5-day return is predicted to be positive due to strong labor market momentum and reduced recession risk.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 160,000 AND UNRATE < 4.0 in the same month
regime_hint: labor market expansion with low unemployment
failure_condition: Over 8 such co-occurrences, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).
